JSON: Name: anatomy_to_tract_mapping Title: Anatomy-conditioned variational generative modeling to infer subject-specific white matter bundle streamlines from T1-weighted MRI without diffusion-based propagation Short Hypothesis: Conditioning a variational generative streamline model on subject T1-weighted MRI produces white-matter bundle reconstructions with higher bundle-shape similarity and connectomic correlation to diffusion-derived reference tractograms than atlas-warping or diffusion-free population methods on the TractoInferno benchmark. Related Work: Existing approaches to white-matter mapping fall into three categories: (1) diffusion-based streamline propagation (deterministic, probabilistic, and global) that integrate local fiber orientation estimates but are sensitive to dMRI SNR, crossing/bottleneck ambiguities, and seeding strategies; (2) supervised segmentation/orientation mapping methods that predict voxelwise tract masks or orientation fields from dMRI or from dMRI-derived features but still depend on local orientation propagation and dMRI quality; (3) generative streamline synthesis using latent-space models (autoencoders, VAEs) or KDE-based sampling which can synthesize bundle-shaped streamlines without stepwise propagation but typically depend on seed streamline quality, population templates, or do not condition on subject anatomy. Limitations across these approaches include susceptibility to orientation ambiguities in regions of crossing/kissing/bending fibers, reduced robustness when dMRI quality is low or absent, limited subject-specificity when using population atlases or warped templates, and generation of spurious streamlines when latent sampling is unconstrained. No prior method combines anatomical conditioning from T1-weighted MRI with a bundle-level variational generative model and density-based latent sampling to directly synthesize subject-specific, anatomically plausible streamlines without pointwise propagation. Abstract: We address the problem of reconstructing subject-specific white matter bundles without relying on diffusion-weighted MRI by proposing an anatomy-conditioned variational generative framework. The method learns a joint mapping from T1-weighted anatomical scans and curated bundle tractograms to a conditioned latent space in which bundle-specific streamline embeddings are modeled with kernel density estimates. At inference the trained encoders extract anatomical features from an input T1 image, sample latent vectors from the conditioned KDE, and decode complete streamlines for each bundle; output streamlines are filtered and trimmed by anatomically derived tissue masks and surfaces. The main contribution is a diffusion-free pipeline that directly synthesizes anatomically plausible, bundle-specific streamlines guided by subject anatomy. Expected outcomes include improved bundle-shape similarity, tract orientation agreement, and connectomic alignment relative to atlas-warping and population-only generation methods, and robust bundle reconstructions in settings with limited or absent diffusion data. Experiments: Datasets: (a) TractoInferno benchmark: 284 subjects; use official splits: training=198, validation=58, test=28; T1w scans intensity-normalized and registered to MNI152 1mm; curated ground-truth bundles from ensemble tractography used as reference. (b) Low-field clinical dataset: 87 64 mT T1w scans with 11 paired 3T scans for limited cross-modality evaluation; 1.6×1.6×5 mm and 1.5×1.5×5 mm upsampled to 1 mm for inference. Baselines: MRtrix probabilistic whole-brain tractography + BundleSeg (dhollander response, iFOD1, seeding at WM-GM interface, generate 3M streamlines then segment bundles), SCIL WM atlas warping to subject space, ATM-Population (apply trained model to population-averaged T1w template then warp to subject), TractSeg-based bundle generation (2000 streamlines per bundle). Model and training: conditional VAE with FiLM-conditioning of anatomical features; KDE per-bundle over latent embeddings; training hyperparameters: Adam lr=1e-4, epochs=1000, batch sampling of K=128 points per streamline, loss weights λ_seg=1, λ_vae=1, λ_adj=1, β=1. Inference variants: generate N={3000,6000,9000} streamlines per bundle. Preprocessing: FreeSurfer white-matter surface extraction, ANTs non-linear registration to MNI152, intensity normalization to [0,1]. Filtering: remove streamlines outside brain mask, length<20 mm, trim points outside white-matter surface except brainstem/cerebellum connectors. Evaluation metrics: bundle adjacency (BUAN) for shape similarity; Tractometer: Dice, overlap, overreach; streamline validity: VS and IS ratios; directional agreement: angular correlation coefficient (ACC) between tract orientation density maps; geometric APDs for mean length, span, volume, surface area; connectomics: Pearson correlation of streamline-count connectomes (DKT parcellation), network density, characteristic path length (CPL), global efficiency, modularity. Statistical analysis: paired two-sided t-tests across subjects for metric comparisons, report mean±SD and 95% CI; report per-bundle violin plots and paired-difference heatmaps. Ablation studies: (A1) remove anatomical conditioning (VAE trained unconditional) to measure anatomy contribution; (A2) replace KDE sampling with isotropic Gaussian prior sampling from N(0,I); (A3) disable adjacent-point regularizer L_ADJ; (A4) disable filtering/trimming pipeline; (A5) vary training data size: train on 50% and 100% of training subjects. Domain generalization tests: evaluate models trained on TractoInferno healthy data on low-field clinical scans and on the 11 paired 3T scans; report metric degradation. Compute profiling: measure inference time and memory to generate 3000 streamlines per bundle on a GPU and on CPU. Reproducibility: release code, trained weights, and fixed random seeds; use same bundle definitions (SCIL) for all comparisons. Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: latent-space sampling may generate spurious or anatomically implausible streamlines leading to increased overreach and false positive connectivity; KDE estimation can overfit to training bundle samples causing poor generalization to unseen anatomical variants; insufficient anatomical encoding can cause missed terminations or inaccurate pathway curvature. Data and evaluation biases: TractoInferno training data are derived from curated tractography on healthy adult subjects and may under-represent pediatric, elderly, or pathological anatomies, causing distribution shift and biased performance estimates; atlas-based bundle definitions used as ground truth inherit labeling choices and may not reflect absolute anatomical truth. Scalability and compute: per-bundle KDEs and generation of thousands of streamlines per bundle increase memory and CPU/GPU usage; generating larger streamline counts or adding many bundles may be computationally expensive for clinical deployment. Limits to generalization: model trained on healthy single-shell or multi-site dMRI-derived bundle references may not generalize to brains with lesions, resection cavities, tumors, or major morphological deformation; the method infers macroscopic pathway geometry from T1 anatomy and cannot recover microstructural orientation information (e.g., crossing-fiber densities) available in diffusion data. Preprocessing sensitivity: performance depends on accurate non-linear registration to MNI space and reliable white-matter surface extraction; registration or segmentation errors propagate into generated bundles. Evaluation limits: diffusion-derived reference tractograms contain their own false positives/negatives; improvements relative to these references do not guarantee ground-truth anatomical correctness.
